node-1.label: Chest pain while breathing and shortness of breath, with difficulty walking even 20 steps

node-2.label: A 26-year-old male visited Korean Medicine Hospital for acute indigestion, initially presenting with tenderness and midback pain after lunch.

node-3.label: Social history includes smoking 0.1 box/day and alcohol consumption 1 time/month, 2 bottles of soju.

node-4.label: The chest pain and shortness of breath occurred after acupuncture treatment and symptoms persisted.

why.why: The Radiologist analysis directly verifies acupuncture-related hemopneumothorax, which necessarily includes pneumothorax; chest X-ray showing a right lung abnormality and CT confirming air in the chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage, together with the temporal relationship after acupuncture, confirm pneumothorax after acupuncture. Missing physical examination and acupuncture details do not override the decisive imaging, so confidence is increased from 0.95 to 0.97.

Radiologist analysis indicates acute cardiopulmonary event is less likely given atypical GI onset; CT-confirmed air and blood in the chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage is diagnostic of acupuncture-related hemopneumothorax and better explains the symptoms. Smoking/alcohol history provides only baseline cardiovascular risk, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.05.

node-7.label: GI disorder with referred chest pain

why.why: Chest X-ray right lung abnormality and CT-confirmed air and blood in the chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage directly support a thoracic cause, not a GI disorder with referred chest pain. Persistent post-acupuncture respiratory symptoms are atypical for GI origin, so confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.02.

node-8.label: Chest X-ray shows right lung abnormality

node-9.label: CT confirms air and blood in the chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage

why.why: The Radiologist analysis directly verifies acupuncture-related hemopneumothorax: CT confirms air and blood in the chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage, and chest X-ray shows a right lung abnormality. The temporal relationship with acupuncture supports causation. Although physical examination and acupuncture details are missing, the expert explicitly states these do not override the decisive imaging findings, reducing the need for further clinical correlation; confidence is increased from 0.9 to 0.96.
